target_customer: Ecommerce and DTC merchants moving $1M or more per month in payments, plus privacy minded stablecoin users and builders of AI agent payments
problem: Wallets and payment processors are slow, route payments to maximise their own take, hold customer keys and leak financial data. Fire offers a non-custodial encrypted wallet with built-in payment processing.
business_model: Payment processing and routing fees on a non-custodial wallet; exact pricing not found
product_category: Non-custodial stablecoin wallet and payment processing

founders.name: Joshua Goldbard
founders.background_notes: YC page says he knows cryptography and telecom. A third-party profile credits MobileCoin co-founding with Shane Glynn, whereas the Fire Wallet launch post says Josh and Manuel led its creation; roles in MobileCoin differ by source.

founders.name: Manuel San Agustin
founders.background_notes: YC page says he co-created MobileCoin with Goldbard.

founders.name: Michael Divine
education: Left college after two years (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Painter, graphic and web designer, internationally exhibited, two published art books per YC page.

competitors.name: MoonPay Agents
competitors.what: Non-custodial layer where AI agents create wallets, trade onchain and cash out to fiat
competitors.traction_then: Launched early 2026 by an established crypto payments company

competitors.name: Coinbase Agentic Wallets
competitors.what: Wallet infrastructure for AI agents on the x402 standard

technical_complexity.rationale: End to end encryption, multi-chain non-custodial key handling, routing and fiat ramps need strong cryptography and compliance integration; the founders say they previously deployed cryptography on tens of millions of devices.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded wallets and agent payment products exist and non-custodial wallets are easy to copy; the founders' MobileCoin credibility is the main edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents launched agent wallet products in 2026. No later outcome is known.

market_need_then: Stablecoin payments and agentic commerce were growing in 2026; the company cites an enterprise customer at about $1.5M per month and a letter of intent, both self-reported.

branding.domain_note: Uses fire.co, a short .co domain; acquisition history not found

identity.logo: Fire logo with flame emoji in launch post
identity.visual_style: Design led by an artist founder, per YC page
identity.voice_and_tone: Privacy as dignity: Your money. Your rules.

brand_strength.rationale: Short memorable name with a clear privacy message, but search results show many unrelated Fire wallets, FIRE tokens and a Chrome extension called Fire Wallet, so it is confusable and no press about the brand exists.

outcome_analysis: Fire Wallet is a Fall 2026 YC company with founders who previously built MobileCoin, giving unusual founder market fit in privacy focused crypto payments. It has early claimed traction and a crowded competitive field with large players launching agent wallets. No outcome news exists yet and no verified funding was found.
notes: Only funding figure is a $125K seed on Dealroom (AI generated profile, no investors visible), unverified and likely the YC standard deal; not recorded as a round. YC page claims MobileCoin was acquired in 2026; not independently verified. Another profile says MobileCoin became Sentz in 2023. Founded year not stated by sources. Founder education beyond Divine not found.
